scope: Curated subset of the C++ STL that recurs in the fmt corpus + canonical samples. ~30 entries in v0; ~50 deferred entries fill in as fmt extractions surface unmapped types.
notes: Per ADR-026, this table is shipped as in-prompt context with every C++ extraction call. The cpp-extract prompts treat the `dotnet_equivalent` / `java_equivalent` columns as authoritative; missing types should be raised as OpenQuestion. The `lifetime_default` column hints which object_lifetimes model the LLM should assume when the source doesn't make ownership explicit.

entries.semantics_notes: C++ string is mutable + value-typed; .NET / Java strings are immutable + reference-typed. Mutation patterns (s += '...') in C++ need to translate to StringBuilder in Java / .NET when in a hot path; otherwise the immutable string is the right default.
entries.thread_safety: Not thread-safe; concurrent mutation is UB. Both targets' immutable string types are inherently thread-safe.

entries.semantics_notes: Non-owning view. Borrowed lifetime — caller must outlive the view. Translation typically copies into an owned String at the call site UNLESS the lifetime is obviously bounded.
entries.thread_safety: Safe for concurrent read (view is immutable); the underlying buffer's mutation is the caller's concern.

entries.semantics_notes: Dynamic array. Iterator invalidation on resize is a recurrent edge_case — both targets' List don't expose iterators in the same way so the translation usually elides this concern.
entries.thread_safety: Not thread-safe in C++; .NET List and Java ArrayList match (use ConcurrentBag / CopyOnWriteArrayList for concurrent variants).

entries.semantics_notes: Famous proxy-reference gotcha — operator[] returns a proxy, not a bool&. Idiomatic translations use the bit-set types instead; misuses become edge_case claims.
Compile-time size. The N parameter doesn't translate to a runtime constraint in either target; if N matters for correctness, raise an Open Question.
Ordered map (red-black tree). Iteration order is sorted — preserve this in translations or callers will silently get wrong-order output.
Hash table. Iteration order is unspecified in C++ but reproducible in both targets within a single run.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: T (owned by value, type must implement IDisposable)
entries.semantics_notes: Sole ownership; destroyed on scope exit. The canonical RAII type. Maps to using-blocks in .NET and try-with-resources in Java.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: T (shared; .NET GC handles it) + manual ref-count when explicit
entries.java_equivalent: T (shared; JVM GC handles it) + manual ref-count when explicit
entries.semantics_notes: Shared ownership. Both targets' garbage collectors make explicit ref-counting unnecessary UNLESS the source uses the ref count semantically (weak_ptr cycle breaking, atomic ops on the count).
Non-owning observer of a shared_ptr. Both targets' WeakReference is the canonical equivalent.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: T? (Nullable<T> for value types; reference types are nullable by default)
entries.semantics_notes: Either a T or no value. Both targets' equivalents differ from std::optional in subtle ways — Java's Optional is not meant to be a field type; .NET's nullable is. Note in the spec if the source uses Optional as a member field.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: sealed type hierarchy + C# 12 pattern matching
entries.java_equivalent: sealed interface (Java 17+) + switch pattern OR Object fallback
entries.semantics_notes: Tagged union. Neither target has a built-in equivalent for arity > 2 — for fmt's purposes (~5 visitor arms), sealed hierarchies work but lose the constexpr-visit optimisation. Larger arms = Open Question.
Heterogeneous record. .NET tuples are clean; Java records (16+) are the modern equivalent.
Two-element heterogeneous record. Often used as map node type; preserve when translating map iteration.
Type-erased callable. Both targets have functional-interface analogues; the arity determines which one (Function for 1 input, BiFunction for 2, etc.).
Type-erased opaque holder. Both targets' Object is the obvious mapping; any_cast<T>() becomes pattern matching.

entries.java_equivalent: T[] + length OR java.nio.ByteBuffer for byte spans
entries.semantics_notes: Non-owning contiguous view. Borrowed lifetime; same caveat as string_view about caller-outlives-view.

entries.java_equivalent: byte (signed in Java; explicit & 0xFF when needed)
entries.semantics_notes: Strongly-typed byte (since C++17). Java's byte is signed which catches translations relying on unsigned semantics.
Stream-based string assembly. Translations usually swap to direct StringBuilder; the iostream operator chaining doesn't translate.
Cross-platform path manipulation. Both targets have clean equivalents; preserve the separator-agnostic semantics.
Time interval. All three have equivalent fixed-precision representations; convert at boundaries.
OS thread. Modern translations usually pick the Task / CompletableFuture analogues for managed cancellation.
Mutual exclusion. .NET's `lock` keyword is the idiomatic translation; Java's `synchronized` is the keyword-level equivalent.

Format string + variadic args. The fmt corpus's own format spec differs from .NET / Java in placeholder syntax — preserve the public API's spec exactly; the implementation can use the target's native formatter.
